# Welcome to IJCAI

International Joint Conferences on Artificial Intelligence is a non-profit corporation founded in California, in 1969 for scientific and educational purposes, including dissemination of information on Artificial Intelligence at conferences in which cutting-edge scientific results are presented and through dissemination of materials presented at these meetings in form of Proceedings, books, video recordings, and other educational materials. IJCAI consists of two divisions: the [Conference Division](https://www.ijcai.org/future_conferences) and the [AI Journal Division](https://aij.ijcai.org/) . IJCAI conferences present premier international gatherings of AI researchers and practitioners and they were held biennially in odd-numbered years since 1969.

Starting with 2016, IJCAI conferences are held annually.
[IJCAI-ECAI-26](https://2026.ijcai.org) will be held in Bremen, Germany from August 15th until August 21st. Locations and dates of other future conferences will be announced officially at the preceding conference.

IJCAI is governed by the [Board of Trustees](http://www.ijcai.org/trustees/current_trustees) , with [IJCAI Secretariat](http://www.ijcai.org/officers/ijcai_secretariat) in charge of its operations.

[IJCAI-25](https://2025.ijcai.org) was held from August 16th until August 22, 2025 in Montreal, Canada and from August 29th until Augst 31st, 2025 in Guangzhou, China. The [Conference Committee](https://2025.ijcai.org/conference-committee/) thanks you all for participating.

# Bremen Officially Confirmed as Host City for IJCAI-ECAI 2026 – World’s Leading AI Conference Coming to Bremen in August 2026

09/05/2025 | Press release

At the close of this year’s International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI), held from August 11–17, 2025 in Montreal, Canada, and August 29–31, 2025 in Guangzhou, China, the official announcement was made: The next edition of the prestigious conference – IJCAI-ECAI 2026 – will take place in Bremen from August 15 to 21, 2026. Around 3,500 to 4,000 AI experts from around the globe are expected to gather in the Hanseatic city during the conference week.

© Erstellt mit Google Gemini

IJCAI, one of the world’s oldest and most renowned conferences on artificial intelligence (AI), will be held next year in conjunction with the European Conference on Artificial Intelligence (ECAI).
The IJCAI-ECAI is a high-level academic conference where leading international researchers and industry representatives come together to share and discuss the latest breakthroughs in cutting-edge AI research. The event is specifically aimed at a scientific audience.

Local organization will be handled by the Local Arrangements Committee (LAC). A team of dedicated scientists and science managers, led by Chairs Prof. Dr.-Ing. Tanja Schultz (University of Bremen) and Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. Frank Kirchner (University of Bremen and German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence, DFKI), along with Co-Chair Dr.-Ing. Monika Michaelis (U Bremen Research Alliance) will coordinate preparations and organization of IJCAI-ECAI 2026 in Bremen.

The conference will kick off with workshops and tutorials from August 15 to 17, 2026 at the University of Bremen. The main conference will begin on August 18, 2026, and take place at the Bremen Exhibition Center.
Simultaneously, an exhibition will feature sponsors along with further industry partners, startups, and scientific institutions.

Prof. Dr. Jutta Günther, Chairperson of the U Bremen Research Alliance and President of the University of Bremen, emphasizes:

> “The fact that one of the world’s most prestigious AI research conferences is coming to Bremen is a major milestone for AI research at our scientific location. What sets Bremen apart is the strategic connection between university-based fundamental research and non-university applied research. We look forward to welcoming researchers and experts from around the world in 2026.”
> 
> 

Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI), Prof. Dr. Antonio Krüger, remarks:

> “I am very pleased that Bremen will host IJCAI-ECAI 2026. This achievement is a great honor for Bremen as a location for AI and at the same time a strong signal of the international visibility of German AI research.

However, in response to the accelerating pace of AI research, particularly in machine learning and related subfields, IJCAI transitioned to an annual format starting in 2016. The first annual conference, IJCAI-16, was held in New York City from July 9–15, 2016, marking a deliberate shift to enable more frequent sharing of breakthroughs amid the growing volume of AI innovations. ## Organization and Governance

### IJCAI Organization Structure

The International Joint Conferences on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI) operates as a non-profit corporation incorporated in the State of California on October 19, 1977, with its principal office in Menlo Park, San Mateo County, though its founding traces back to 1969 for scientific and educational purposes related to artificial intelligence dissemination.

### Collaboration with National Societies

The International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI) operates under a joint sponsorship model, where conferences are co-organized with national AI societies to promote global representation and shared expertise. Under this framework, national AI organizations, such as the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) in the United States and the European Association for Artificial Intelligence (EurAI) in Europe, propose and co-host events in a rotational pattern across regions. [[[8]]()]() This approach ensures that hosting duties rotate among societies from different continents, fostering diverse perspectives in AI research and application.
[[[8]]()]() The hosting process involves a formal bidding mechanism open exclusively to established AI scientific societies worldwide, excluding submissions from congress centers, professional organizers, or government entities. Bidders must outline their capacity to manage logistics, secure venues, and align with IJCAI's standards for academic quality and inclusivity; successful proposals receive oversight, branding support, and resources from the IJCAI Organization to facilitate execution. [[[8]]()]() For instance, calls for bids are issued periodically, with the next open invitation for IJCAI-2027 and IJCAI-2028 conferences targeting societies globally, emphasizing regions with growing AI communities. [[[8]]()]() Recent examples illustrate this collaboration's role in diversifying locations and participation. The 2024 conference (IJCAI-24) was held in Jeju, South Korea, co-sponsored by a national AI society to highlight regional advancements in intelligent systems.

[[[28]]()]() For instance, IJCAI 2022 accepted 679 out of 4,537 submissions (15%), while IJCAI 2024 accepted 791 out of 5,651 (14%). [[[20]]()]() This selectivity has remained consistently below 20% from 2017 to 2022, establishing IJCAI as a high-quality benchmark for AI research. [[[28]]()]() Accepted papers are published in the official IJCAI proceedings, available open-access via the conference website (ijcai.org), and indexed in major academic databases such as DBLP, Scopus, and Google Scholar. [[[29]]()]() There are no page charges for authors, facilitating broader participation. [[[30]]()]() Post-conference, resources including presentation videos and slides from technical sessions are made publicly available on the IJCAI website to extend the reach of disseminated knowledge.
[[[1]]()]() Selected works may also contribute to special issues in affiliated journals like Artificial Intelligence (AIJ), which is sponsored by the IJCAI organization. [[[31]]()]()

## Awards

### Lifetime Achievement Awards

The International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI) bestows two prominent lifetime achievement awards to honor enduring contributions to the field: the IJCAI Award for Research Excellence and the Donald E. Walker Distinguished Service Award. These awards recognize senior scientists for their sustained impact over decades, selected annually by the IJCAI Board of Trustees based on recommendations from an Awards Selection Committee and input from an Awards Review Committee comprising former trustees, advisory members, recent program chairs, and past recipients. Nominations are open to the AI community and emphasize a career-long record of excellence, with one recipient per award per conference.
[[[32]]()]() The IJCAI Award for Research Excellence, established in 1985, celebrates scientists who have maintained a program of consistently high-quality research yielding substantial results in artificial intelligence throughout their careers. It highlights foundational figures whose work has profoundly shaped AI subfields, such as knowledge representation, machine learning, and reasoning. The award is presented at the conference, where recipients deliver a distinguished lecture. Notable past recipients include John McCarthy (1985) for pioneering AI as a field, Judea Pearl (1999) for advances in Bayesian networks and causality, Geoffrey E. Hinton (2005) for contributions to neural networks, and more recent honorees like Stuart Russell (2022) for work in AI safety and search algorithms, and Rina Dechter (2025) for seminal developments in constraint satisfaction and probabilistic inference. ## Impact and Significance

### Influence on AI Field

Since its inception in 1969, the International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI) has served as a premier venue for advancing AI research, establishing key trends across subfields such as early logic programming in the 1970s and more recent developments in deep learning since the 2010s. [[[1]]()]() [[[39]]()]() By providing a platform for presenting groundbreaking work, IJCAI has influenced the direction of AI methodologies, from symbolic AI paradigms to neural network architectures, fostering innovations that permeate subsequent research agendas.
[[[40]]()]() IJCAI's proceedings, spanning over 50 years, form a comprehensive archive cited in thousands of subsequent papers, significantly impacting funding decisions, academic careers, and industry adoption of AI technologies. [[[1]]()]() [[[39]]()]() With an h5-index of 136 as of 2023, it consistently ranks among the top AI conferences, underscoring its role in shaping career trajectories through prestigious publications and awards. [[[41]]()]() These metrics highlight IJCAI's enduring influence on resource allocation in AI, where acceptance often signals high-potential contributions worthy of investment. [[[42]]()]() The conference's global reach bridges academia and industry through international hosting in diverse locations and collaborative programs, while promoting diversity via dedicated activities and inclusive policies.
